title: What kind of reader are you, really?
dek: TBR hoarder, abandoner, rereader, spoiler-first, audiobook convert, library loyalist, slow reader or margin scribbler. Twelve questions about the books you finish and the ones you don't.

questions.prompt: The bookshop closes in ten minutes. You came in for one specific book.

options.label: Find it, then browse the same shelf for forty minutes
Buy it plus two others you'll start tonight
Check if the library has it first
Leave with something else entirely

questions.prompt: There's a book on your shelf with a bookmark at page 58. It's been there since March.

options.label: Restart it. Properly this time
Pick up exactly where you stopped
Give it away. It had its chance
Read the ending to see if it's worth it
Finish every book you start
Remember everything perfectly

questions.prompt: A book you abandon says more about you than one you finish.
I have bought a book because of how it looked on the table.
Someone tells you the ending of the book you're halfway through.

options.label: Pretend you already knew
Ask them to keep going, ruin it properly
Never speak to them again (until Thursday)
Finish it tonight out of spite
A chair with good light and a pen nearby
A train, headphones, one chapter per stop
A library table with strangers breathing
The same chair you read it in the first time

questions.prompt: The library has one copy and fourteen people waiting.

options.label: Join the queue. Be patient
Buy it. You'll reread it anyway
Find a copy online, read the first page, decide
Audiobook. Sixteen hours, two walks

questions.prompt: The film should be watched before the book.
A friend asks for a book recommendation.

options.label: The one you've given to five people
Whatever's on your bedside pile
Ask what they liked last, then think
Send the audiobook link

results.name: The Margin Scribbler
results.blurb: A book isn't finished until it's been argued with. You underline, you disagree in the margin and you fold the corner of the page that made you stop. Lending you a book is an act of trust and a request for a response.
results.watchOut: Not every thought needs to be recorded. Read one chapter without a pen.

results.name: The TBR Hoarder
results.blurb: Your pile is a personality and a promise. Buying the book feels like starting it, which is why there are eleven on the floor and one in your bag. You are not behind. You are provisioned.
results.watchOut: The pile is not a to-do list. Read the one you keep picking up.

results.name: The Abandoner
results.blurb: You give a book a fair chance and then you stop. Life is short, the shelf is long, and finishing something you dislike isn't loyalty — it's a chore. People call it quitting. You call it editing.
strengths: Reads more good books than most
results.watchOut: Some books only work after page 100. Give one of them a second night.

results.name: The Rereader
results.tagline: Knows how it ends, goes again
results.blurb: You have a comfort book and you have read it enough times to notice the author's small mistakes. New books are a risk; this one is a conversation with someone you already trust. You're not stuck. You're visiting.
strengths: Finds new meaning in old pages
Loyal in a way people feel
results.watchOut: Comfort is a great holiday and a bad address. Try one new book this month.

results.name: The Spoiler First
results.blurb: You check the ending before you commit, because being surprised is not the same as being satisfied. You want to know the book can carry the weight before you give it a week. People gasp when you admit this. You remain unbothered.
results.watchOut: Some surprises are worth protecting. Let one book surprise you.

results.name: The Audiobook Convert
results.blurb: You read while walking, cooking and pretending to listen to someone. Your library is narrated by people you now think of as friends. You will tell anyone who'll listen that it absolutely counts, because it absolutely does.
strengths: Fits reading into a real life
results.watchOut: Some sentences need to be looked at. Read one chapter with your eyes.

results.name: The Library Loyalist
results.blurb: You will wait eleven weeks rather than buy the hardback. The library is not a fallback, it's the whole system, and you have opinions about the reservation queue. You've read more than anyone and spent almost nothing.
results.watchOut: The wait is also a way of not deciding. Treat yourself to the new one.

results.name: The Slow Reader
results.blurb: You read one book at a time, slowly, and you finish it. No pile, no pressure, no annual target. It takes you three weeks and you remember all of it, which is more than the people bragging about fifty books can say.
results.watchOut: Slow is fine. Stopped is different. Pick it up tonight, just one page.
